name: Capacitor-Grade BOPP/Dielectric Films
scope: Ultra-thin metallised BOPP/PET dielectric film for film capacitors (EV inverters and chargers, solar/wind inverters, grid capacitor banks, drives) and the Indian listed companies making, buying or adjacent to it.

summary.one_line: Four Indian listed companies now have company-confirmed capacitor-film capacity: Xpro India, Cosmo First, Jindal Poly (through JPFL Films) and SRF. New this edition: Xpro India, which we had missed. It is the only one that reports dielectric-film revenue (Rs 135.5 cr in FY26, about 27% of its sales), and it doubled its Indian line capacity in March 2026. No company-level catalyst landed this week; Q2 FY27 results are the next check.
key_points: IndexBox (28 Sep 2026) forecasts 6-9% annual growth in global dielectric capacitor-film demand over 2026-2035 (7.5% base case). It expects automotive power electronics to grow fastest, at 10-14% a year (S1). Mordor's forecast for finished plastic film capacitors is slower: USD 2.58 bn in 2026 to USD 3.27 bn in 2031, a 4.86% CAGR (S2).

New this edition: Xpro India commissioned a new dielectric-film line at Barjora on 27 Mar 2026, taking Indian nameplate capacity from 4,000 to 8,000 MT a year (S21). A 5,000 MTPA UAE line is due in FY27, for a target of 13,000 MT by 2027 (S20, S21). FY26 dielectric volume was 3,541 MT and net sales Rs 135.52 cr, broadly flat on FY25 (S20).

SRF: ICICI Direct's Q1 FY27 call notes (24 Jul 2026) say trial runs are complete and customer approvals are progressing well. Commercial sales are expected during FY27, with near-full utilisation targeted by Q1-Q2 FY28 (S12). Phase 1 of the Indore plant (~Rs 277 cr) was commissioned on 15 May 2026 (S11).

Cosmo First has made metallised capacitor-grade BOPP (2.5-12 micron) since Dec 2023, launched at ~750 MT/yr (S3). Its website still rates the metalliser at 900 MT/yr and says a second metalliser is being prepared; no launch date is given (S4). The Q1 FY27 presentation's strategy slide does not mention capacitor film (S23).

CRISIL (18 May 2026) puts JPFL Films' operational capacitor-film capacity at 5,000 TPA after the May 2025 Nashik fire (S10). The Rs 250 cr doubling announced in 2024 (S5) is still not confirmed as complete.
ECMS approvals include three capacitor-film projects: SRF (polypropylene capacitor film, Rs 496 cr) (S13), Dhruv Industries (S14) and Capfilm India (S15). We found no new ECMS tranche this week.

Jindal Poly has two open SEBI show-cause notices, dated 27 Apr 2026 (S9) and 6 Aug 2026 (S8). The company says the financial impact cannot be ascertained (S8), and CRISIL has its ratings on Watch Negative (S10).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Xpro India has the most direct exposure: dielectric film was Rs 135.52 cr of Rs 505.49 cr FY26 operating revenue (S20, S21), and capacity is being lifted to 13,000 MT by 2027 (S21). The market already pays for this: on Screener the stock trades at 75.2x P/E and 3.23x book (S22).
SRF has new dedicated capacity. Trials are complete and commercial sales are expected in FY27 (S12). The business is small next to Rs 17,001 cr of trailing sales (S19).

Cosmo First has made the film longest among diversified packaging-film makers (since Dec 2023), and its 'series' grade targets EV and renewable-energy inverters (S3, S4). At 12.8x P/E and 1.32x book (S17), the stock shows no capacitor premium.

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Polypropylene resin makes up 50-65% of production cost, and China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1). That limits pricing power for Indian entrants.

Domestic supply is ramping up quickly. Xpro (4,000 to 13,000 MT), SRF, JPFL (5,000 TPA) and Cosmo are all adding capacity (S10, S12, S21, S4), against domestic demand that no source we found quantifies. Prices could fall as these lines fill.
Jindal Poly's governance risk: two 2026 SEBI notices (S8, S9), CRISIL ratings on Watch Negative, and Rs ~1,125 cr infused into JPFL since the fire (S10). Its trailing net loss is Rs 991 cr (S18).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Q2 FY27 results (dates not yet announced):SRF's first capacitor-film sales (S12), Xpro's Barjora ramp-up and UAE trial run (S20, S21), and any capacitor-film disclosure from Cosmo (S23).
Commissioning of Cosmo's second metalliser (S4) and confirmation of JPFL's capacitor-film doubling (S5, S10).
Replies to and outcomes of the SEBI notices at Jindal Poly (S8, S9).
Government notification of DGTR's 29-30 Sep 2026 PET-film anti-dumping recommendation (S24). No capacitor-BOPP-specific duty has been found.

kpis.label: Xpro India India nameplate capacity
kpis.sub: after 27 Mar 2026 line; 13,000 MT target by 2027 (S21)

blocks.text: Capacitor-grade film is an ultra-thin dielectric film (the insulating layer between a capacitor's plates), mostly biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP). It is vacuum-metallised with aluminium or aluminium-zinc and wound into film capacitors. Cosmo First makes it in clean-room conditions with micro-slitting, at 2.5-12 micron, for AC and DC capacitors (S3). Xpro India makes 2-16 micron base film in standard and high-temperature grades, focused on ultra-thin, hazy and semi-rough films for power capacitors, EV systems and railways (S20). Packaging BOPP is thicker and has none of these purity or surface requirements. The thin metal layer also gives self-healing: a local short burns the metal away instead of destroying the capacitor.

Film makers are moving to thinner substrates that withstand higher voltages: IndexBox cites 2-4 micron grades for automotive use, especially 800-volt EV platforms. It sees BOPP holding 60-70% of volume and metallised film 40-50% of value (S1). Xpro describes the demand as 'structural, not cyclical', driven by electrification, renewables, grid modernisation and traction (S20).

blocks.caption: Third-party forecasts (each is the publisher's own forecast)

blocks.text: The two forecasts measure different things: IndexBox measures film demand, Mordor the value of finished capacitors. We could not open the Future Market Insights figure, so it is left out.

When it launched in Dec 2023, Cosmo said capacitor film was largely imported from China and saw room for both import substitution and exports (S3). China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1). Xpro calls itself the first-mover domestic producer and expects to remain India's largest by capacity (S20). We found no official tonnage series for India's capacitor-film imports.

DGTR's final findings (29-30 Sep 2026) recommend anti-dumping duties of USD 54-366/t on PET film from Bangladesh, China and Thailand. They take effect only if the government notifies them, and as of 13 Oct we found no such notification (S24). The case covers PET film; BOPP, the main capacitor dielectric, is not included (S1).

blocks.text: After the Aug 2026 tranche, ECMS had 106 approved applications with Rs 69,548 cr of investment, and 38 plants were producing (S15). Metallisers and capacitor makers approved under the scheme add domestic demand for base film. We found no new tranche in the week to 13 Oct.

blocks.title: Xpro India dielectric film nameplate capacity
blocks.source: Source: Xpro India FY26 annual report via FilingReader and IIFL (S20, S21)

blocks.text: Xpro India: its dielectric volume was 3,541 MT in FY26 versus 3,556 MT in FY25, with net sales of Rs 135.52 cr versus Rs 136.34 cr. Volumes were flat because the new line started only at year-end (S20). That makes dielectric film about 27% of the Rs 505.49 cr operating revenue (our calculation from S20, S21). FY26 PAT was Rs 30.52 cr after an Rs 11.14 cr unrealised forex translation loss (S21). Girish Behal is proposed as MD from 1 Jan 2027 (S21).

SRF: ICICI Direct's call notes say commercial capacitor-film sales are expected during FY27 (S12). The board has also approved Rs 250 cr for a 25,000 MTPA BOPET thick-film line for electrical and electronics uses, and capacitor-grade BOPP is part of a stated shift away from commodity thin films (S12). Set against SRF's Rs 17,001 cr trailing sales (S19), the capacitor plant is small.

Cosmo First: the capacitor range covers Al-Zn standard, pure Al, slope/RMF, segmented and 'series' metallised PP films. The company says the series grade targets drives, renewable-energy inverters, UPS and EVs (S4). In Q1 FY27, net revenue was Rs 1,166 cr and net debt Rs 1,166 cr (2.3x EBITDA). The company says its capex cycle is complete and film utilisation is about 85% (S23). It discloses no capacitor-film revenue.

Jindal Poly Films: CRISIL says JPFL had 5,000 TPA of capacitor capacity before the fire and 5,000 TPA operational now. It also reports a 9M FY26 operating loss of Rs 51 cr on Rs 1,696 cr of operating income, and says the loss of profits is not covered by insurance (S10). Screener shows a trailing net loss of Rs 991 cr (S18).
Xpro India is the only one of the four that reports capacitor-film volume and revenue separately. Any capacitor-film share for SRF, Cosmo or Jindal Poly is an estimate.

items: Universal Cables makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and power-factor panels, so it is a potential domestic film buyer (S6). We found no disclosed film-supply tie-up.
Polyplex lists electrical insulation among its BOPET uses, but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S25). The PET-film anti-dumping recommendation matters more for it (S24).
UFlex / Flex Films makes BOPP, BOPET, CPP and metallised packaging films; we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S16).
Garware Hi-Tech Films makes polyester film for electrical and motor insulation at 10-350 micron (S7), thicker than the 2-16 micron capacitor band (S20).

blocks.text: Coverage gap: the main domestic film-capacitor makers (TDK India, Vishay India, Deki) and the ECMS metallisers (Dhruv, Capfilm) are unlisted or not confirmed as listed (S14, S15). The listed producers are small caps (Xpro, Cosmo, Jindal Poly) plus one large cap (SRF) where the business is immaterial. We found no mid-cap pure play.

sections.title: Research house views and market pricing

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.title: Price-to-book of confirmed capacitor-film producers, 12 Oct 2026

blocks.text: Valuations split along exposure. Xpro, the only producer with large and disclosed exposure, trades at 75.2x trailing earnings (S22), so the market is paying for the theme there. Cosmo First (12.8x) and Jindal Poly (below book) are priced on packaging-film earnings and, for Jindal Poly, governance (S17, S18).

Broker coverage: ICICI Direct's SRF result note (24 Jul 2026) discusses capacitor-grade BOPP only as part of SRF's shift to specialty films (S12). We found no Indian broker note built around capacitor film. Media coverage is mostly trade-press launch stories (S3, S5) and results summaries (S21).

items: Resin cost: polypropylene makes up 50-65% of production cost (S1).
Chinese overcapacity: China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1), and most imports came from China (S3).

Domestic supply build-out: Xpro's capacity is going from 4,000 MT to a 13,000 MT target (S21), SRF is ramping up (S12), JPFL has 5,000 TPA running (S10) and Cosmo plans a second metalliser (S4). That is a lot of new supply relative to an unquantified domestic market.
Slow ramp-up: SRF took ~2.5 years from board approval (Oct 2023) to commissioning (May 2026) and targets full utilisation only in FY28 (S11, S12). Xpro's FY26 dielectric volume was flat (S20).
Small share of revenue: commodity packaging-film cycles dominate earnings at Cosmo, Jindal Poly and SRF (S12, S17, S18).
Governance: Jindal Poly faces SEBI notices dated 27 Apr and 6 Aug 2026, addressed to the company, its key managers, promoters and group entities (S8, S9). CRISIL ratings are on Watch Negative (S10).
Q2 FY27 results:SRF's first capacitor-film sales (S12), Xpro's dielectric volumes and Barjora ramp-up (S20).
Trial run and commissioning of Xpro's 5,000 MTPA UAE line (S20, S21).
Commissioning of Cosmo First's second metalliser (S4) and JPFL's capacitor-film doubling (S5, S10).
ECMS metallised-film projects (Dhruv, Capfilm) coming on stream, adding domestic demand for base film (S14, S15).
Localisation of EV and solar inverters, the segment IndexBox expects to grow 10-14% a year (S1).
Government notification of the PET-film anti-dumping duty (S24). No capacitor-BOPP-specific trade action has been found.

companies.name: Xpro India Ltd
companies.role: Dedicated BOPP dielectric (capacitor) base-film maker at Barjora, West Bengal. It makes 2-16 micron grades and reported FY26 dielectric sales of Rs 135.52 cr on 3,541 MT (S20). A new line commissioned on 27 Mar 2026 doubled Indian capacity to 8,000 MT (S21).
companies.impact: Has the most direct exposure among listed names, with a 5,000 MTPA UAE line due in FY27 and a 13,000 MT target (S20, S21). At 75.2x P/E (S22), much of the theme already looks priced in, and more domestic competitors are arriving (S12, S10).

companies.name: Cosmo First Ltd
companies.role: Makes metallised capacitor-grade BOPP (2.5-12 micron). Launched Dec 2023 at ~750 MT/yr (S3); the metalliser is now rated 900 MT/yr, with a second being prepared (S4).
companies.impact: Capacitor film is undisclosed and earnings follow packaging film. The company calls its capex cycle complete, with net debt 2.3x EBITDA (S23); the stock trades at 12.8x P/E (S17).

companies.name: Jindal Poly Films Ltd
companies.role: Its subsidiary JPFL Films makes capacitor film: 5,000 TPA is operational per CRISIL (S10), and a Rs 250 cr doubling was announced in 2024 (S5).
companies.impact: Fire recovery, the trailing loss and two 2026 SEBI notices outweigh the capacitor theme (S8, S9, S10, S18).

companies.name: SRF Ltd
companies.role: Commissioned a capacitor-grade BOPP plant at Indore on 15 May 2026 at ~Rs 277 cr (S11). Holds an ECMS approval for a Rs 496 cr capacitor PP-film project (S13).
companies.impact: Commercial sales are expected in FY27, with near-full utilisation by Q1-Q2 FY28 (S12). Immaterial to group earnings but a new competitor for Xpro, Cosmo and JPFL.

companies.name: Universal Cables Ltd
companies.role: Makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and APFC panels (S6).
companies.impact: A potential domestic film buyer as local supply grows; no film-supply tie-up has been disclosed (S6).

companies.name: Polyplex Corporation Ltd
companies.role: BOPET film maker that lists electrical insulation among its industrial uses (S25).
companies.impact: Adjacent only: no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S25). The PET-film anti-dumping recommendation matters more to it (S24).

companies.name: UFlex Ltd
companies.role: Its Flex Films business makes BOPP, BOPET, CPP and metallised films (S16).
companies.impact: Has metallising know-how, but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S16).

companies.name: Garware Hi-Tech Films Ltd
companies.role: Makes polyester film for electrical and motor insulation at 10-350 micron (S7).
companies.impact: Its range sits above the capacitor-film thickness band (S20), so the theme does not currently apply.

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W41 edition, researched on 13 Oct 2026 with web search and page fetches. Re-checked: SRF, Cosmo First, JPFL/Jindal Poly (SEBI notice of 6 Aug re-fetched), ECMS (no new tranche found) and the PET anti-dumping case (no notification found). Added: Xpro India, a listed dedicated dielectric-film maker that earlier editions missed, sourced from its FY26 MD&A (IIFL extract), FilingReader's annual-report summary and Screener. Also added ICICI Direct's 24 Jul 2026 SRF Q1 FY27 note, which replaces last week's search-result excerpts of SRF's call, and Cosmo's Q1 FY27 investor presentation. Valuations are Screener figures as of 12 Oct 2026, plus 13 Oct for Xpro. Dropped: Volza shipment counts (a weak proxy), the JPFL Rs 700 cr Nashik packaging capex and fire articles (covered by CRISIL; packaging-only), Syrma SGS (no capacitor-film link) and the SRF transcript excerpts. A 2023 DSIJ claim that Xpro met ~33% of domestic demand was not used because it is stale and unsourced. Not confirmed, so not stated as fact: SRF phase-2 capitalisation, JPFL's capacitor doubling, Cosmo's second metalliser, any capacitor-BOPP-specific trade action. Source IDs were renumbered from last week. Some company-website dates are access dates. Companies are classed 'other' unless a company or primary source confirms capacitor-grade production. No ratings or price targets are given.
